# Visualizing Distributions

## Distributions

- How a particular variable is distributed in a dataset
- Statistics: Mean, median, mode, standard deviation, skewness, kurtosis
- Visualizations: Histogram, density plot, boxplot, violin plot

## Histograms

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Filled rectangles
- Bin = Width of rectangle = range of values in that bin
- Height of rectangle = number of observations in that bin
- Bin width matters for storytelling

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-hist", fig_hist(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Density plots

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Curve estimated from the data - smooth version of a histogram
- Area under the curve = 1
- Height of curve = density of observations at that value
- Density interpretation: Probability of observing a value in a given range = area under the curve for that range
- Bandwidth matters for storytelling

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-density", fig_density(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Density plots
:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Pitfall: smooth across gaps in data or where there are no observations.

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-density-bad", fig_density_bad(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```


## Two or more distributions

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Avoid stacked histograms - hard to compare values
- Bars start at different points
- Use side-by-side histograms or density plots instead

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-stacked-histogram", fig_stacked_histogram(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 9, y = 1.4, width = 5)
place_fig("fig_side-histogram", fig_side_histogram(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 9, y = 5, width = 5)
```

## Two or more distributions

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Avoid stacked histograms - hard to compare values
- Bars start at different points
- Use side-by-side histograms or density plots instead

## Two or more distributions

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Density plots extend nicely to more than one distribution
- Use color to separate distributions
- Transparency can help with overlapping distributions

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-four-density", fig_four_density(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```
